3d26b69b60.why: Old leak fixed: 'twice a day' is now 'again, day after day', so fc56f04187 and 1d6b48be1b are no longer given away. Key true (NOAA: 'the moon is the dominant force affecting the Earth's tides'); 'mainly' covers the Sun's share. Wind is the sourced misconception (Kesler Science: 'Tides are caused by wind blowing the water around'); heat and magnetism are live and truly wrong. Choices parallel and similar in length. Core 6th-grade tides fact. Non-blocking: the stems of 1d6b48be1b and 872deb5a0c presuppose the Moon's tides, as any tides unit must; this was so before and the judge accepted it.

1d6b48be1b.why: Old tell fixed: 'too' is gone, and 'up into', shared by the stem and the key only, is gone too; 'Sinking into' kept parallel. Key true (NASA: the oceans bulge 'on both the side closest to the Moon and the side farthest from the Moon'). 'Rising into high water' reads as forming the second bulge, which is right at the grade's level. Lures model the sourced one-bulge belief ('only one high tide per day, on the side of Earth facing the Moon') and are truly wrong. Context true.

8846cf43e0.why: Old dead lure fixed: the Sun-orbits-Earth choice is replaced by the sourced wind misconception, live for a student who thinks wind drives the tides, and false. Key true (NOAA: the Moon 'revolves around the Earth in the same direction that the Earth rotates', so Earth needs an extra 50 minutes to catch up; lunar day 24 hours 50 minutes). 'Earth moves on along its path around the Sun' is truly wrong: the lunar day is Earth's turn relative to the Moon, and Earth's orbit, if anything, trims the slip on clock time. Key and that lure are structural twins, so neither stands out. Context true, with the fact-check's 'daily timing' wording taken.

872deb5a0c.why: Old weak lures fixed: 'only in the daytime' and 'shared out among all the planets' are live naive ideas, and both are false (NASA: the Moon's gravity 'affects the entire Earth, pulling at every point'; the solar tide runs on a 12-hour cycle, so it has a night-side bulge; the pull between two bodies depends only on their masses and distance). 'Made of hot gas' kept and false. Key true: NOAA, Sun 27 million times the Moon's mass, 390 times farther, tidal force 'inversely as the cube of the distance', solar tide about half; 27.1 million / 389 cubed is about 0.46. 'Nearly 400 times' agrees with 52479c8328. The stem still gives mass, so distance is the other thing a student must know, but that is knowledge, not a stem tell. 6th-grade tides content.

754ec2c299.why: Old leak fixed: the stem now defines spring tides by the line-up, not by the highest highs and lowest lows, so 20e142e1f0's key is not given away, and the question asks the simple why (line-up at new and at full moon, so twice a month). Key true: NOAA, 'Spring tides occur twice each lunar month all year long, without regard to the season'; the name has 'nothing to do with the season of spring'. Lures are the sourced season belief and the one-line-up-a-month slip, all live and false. Context's 'around every new moon' taken from the fact-check. Non-blocking: the key sits where the other choices' parts meet ('twice a month', 'all year round'), unchanged from before and not flagged by the judge.
